title: A review row runs each engine in its own agent, so a runner always returns its block

release_levels.reason: fixes a shipped capability: a runner under /vwf:execute all ended its turn on an engine's report and never returned its block
the manual's /vwf:execute passages say how the engines run, and change with the fix

units.title: Engines run in their own agent
A skill's output is never the runner's reply

shared_files.why: human-facing docs that U1's and U2's changes falsify

decisions.decision: How must a review row run the engines (/security-review, /code-review), which end with their own final report?
decisions.ruling: Each engine in a subagent: the orchestrator dispatches one engine agent per engine, in one message. Each invokes its engine through Skill, writes the report verbatim to `<folder>/engine/<loop-id>-<round>.log`, and returns one status line. The engine's final report then ends only that agent's turn. Same for plain `/vwf:execute` and runners, so one path.
decisions.rejected: Instruction only (keep the Skill call in the orchestrator and add text that engine output is data) — the engine's own instructions still tell the model to end with the report; runners only (engine agents only under `all`) — two paths to keep in step

decisions.decision: Which agent runs an engine?
decisions.ruling: A new vwf agent: `plugins/vwf/agents/execute-engine.md`, tools Skill, Agent, Write, Bash, Read. It invokes the named engine with its target, writes the report verbatim to the given log path, and returns one line `ENGINE: <name> <round> ok <path>` or `ENGINE: <name> <round> failed <reason>`. Under `all` it is layer 2 (the loop, the runner, the engine agent); `/code-review`'s own reviewer agents then sit at layer 3, the default nesting limit. It dispatches no agent itself; only the engine it invokes may start its own agents (D12). The layer-3 precedent is plugins/vwf/skills/execute/workflows/all.md:230-231, where the docs-sync surveyor runs at layer 3 in every all run (D15).
decisions.rejected: The built-in general-purpose agent — the contract would live only in review-unit.md's prompt text, and the agent has every tool

decisions.decision: The runner still invokes vwf skills through Skill (git-workflow, backlog, plan-management, handoff), and a skill's closing report could end its turn the same way. What else changes beside D1?
decisions.ruling: Rule in the runner: execute-runner.md and all.md *Runner mode* say that a skill's output — any Skill call, a vwf skill or a built-in — is input for the next step, never the reply. After each Skill call the runner continues the run, and its last message is always the return block. The loop's rule that a reply with no block is STOPPED (all.md *The loop* step 4) stays as it is (the user's rule: fix the source, not a guard).
decisions.rejected: Rule plus a loop resume (the loop resumes a runner once with SendMessage before it records STOPPED) — a guard; D1 only — leaves the same failure open for the vwf skills

decisions.decision: What happens when an engine agent fails?
decisions.ruling: An engine agent that errors, returns no `ENGINE:` line, or returns `failed` counts as an unavailable engine under the rule review-unit.md already has: the reason is kept for the reviewers' prompt. The dispatch replaces only the wait through TaskOutput and TaskStop.
decisions.rejected: A new failure rule for engine agents — the existing rule already says what an unavailable engine means

decisions.decision: The cause the survey found
decisions.ruling: review-unit.md:88 invokes the built-in engines `/code-review` and `/security-review` through the Skill tool, in the orchestrator's own turn. Their closing report ended a runner's turn, so the runner never returned its five-line block, in plans 2026-11-23-bootstrap-value-quoting and 2026-11-26-stackgen-bootstrap-tasks; each time a manual SendMessage resume let the runner finish. No text told the runner that the report is input for the next step, and no hook checks the shape of a runner's last message.

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: No. The plan lands no runnable code: it changes skill prose, an agent definition and docs. The wave review is the check.
decisions.rejected: A security-only review unit — it would review prose

decisions.decision: What proves the fix, beyond the diff?
decisions.ruling: No kept gate. The new agent loads only in a restarted session, so the first real proof is the next `/vwf:execute all` run that reaches a review row after a restart: the runner returns its five-line block with no manual resume.
decisions.rejected: A scratch `all` run inside this plan — the run's session cannot load the agent it adds

decisions.decision: Execution mode
decisions.ruling: teams, by the user's choice: wave 1 holds two edit units (U1 and U2). Under `/vwf:execute all` a runner runs it solo anyway, per all.md *Runner mode*.
decisions.rejected: solo

decisions.decision: How the engine agent reads the worktree, not the main checkout: a subagent shell starts in the session folder
decisions.ruling: cd first. The engine agent first runs `cd <worktree>` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`; a mismatch returns `ENGINE: <name> <round> failed <reason>` and invokes nothing. The in-run proof in U1 was dropped by the user's 'cut to the minimum' ruling (2026-11-28): the risk that the engine's own git commands still read the main checkout is recorded in D20, not proven in this run.
decisions.rejected: A kept gate after landing only: no proof in this run

decisions.decision: The engine agent's return contract (rulings review round 1, gap 1)
decisions.ruling: `ENGINE: <name> <round> ok <path>` or `ENGINE: <name> <round> failed <reason>`: a failed engine wrote no usable log, so the reason is what the report needs. D2 and D9 match.
decisions.rejected: Always end in the log path, with the reason written into the log

decisions.decision: A time limit on an engine agent (gap 2)
decisions.ruling: Reversed by the user's 'cut to the minimum' ruling (2026-11-28): engine agents are dispatched in the foreground, both in one message, as unit agents are, so their one-line replies come back in the same turn. There is no 30-minute wait, no TaskStop and no TaskOutput for the engines. A hung engine hangs the run, as a hung unit agent does (D20).
decisions.rejected: Background agents with a 30-minute wait and TaskStop: a runner cannot be shown to read a background agent's reply (all.md Runner mode: its agents' replies go to the top session); no time limit was the alternative kept.

decisions.decision: The engine agent's tools and its ban on agents (gap 3)
decisions.ruling: Tools: Skill, Agent, Write, Bash, Read. The agent dispatches no agent itself; only the engine it invokes may start its own agents (/code-review starts reviewer agents).
decisions.rejected: No Agent tool: /code-review would fail in the engine agent

decisions.decision: The observable fact that the engine read the worktree (gap 4)
decisions.ruling: Dropped by the user's 'cut to the minimum' ruling (2026-11-28): no in-run D9 proof, so no proof base. The risk is recorded in D20, not proven in this run.
decisions.rejected: Accept as unverified and wait for the first real all run

decisions.decision: What the run does when the D9 check fails (gap 5)
decisions.ruling: Dropped by the user's 'cut to the minimum' ruling (2026-11-28): no in-run D9 proof, so nothing to ask on a failed proof. The risk is recorded in D20.
decisions.rejected: Land with an open gap

decisions.decision: How the layer-3 claim is recorded (gap 6)
decisions.ruling: D2 cites plugins/vwf/skills/execute/workflows/all.md:230-231 and the docs-sync surveyor, which runs at layer 3 in every all run, as the precedent. The first all run with a code-review row is the proof of layer 3, recorded as a known risk in D20.
decisions.rejected: Add a /code-review check to U1: slower, and in a plain run it proves only layer 2

decisions.decision: Owner of the three passages that say the orchestrator runs the engines itself (gaps 7 and 8)
decisions.ruling: U1 owns and edits plugins/vwf/skills/execute/references/rules.md (about :34), plugins/vwf/agents/execute-code-reviewer.md (about :8) and plugins/vwf/agents/execute-security-reviewer.md (about :7): an execute-engine agent runs the engine, and the orchestrator hands over its log.
decisions.rejected: Accept as out of scope: the passages stay partly false

decisions.decision: The two reviewer rows of skills-and-agents.md (gap 9)
decisions.ruling: U3's edit also rewords .claude/skills/vwf-plugin/references/skills-and-agents.md:74-75: an execute-engine agent runs the engine, and the orchestrator hands its log to the reviewer; the reviewers still run none.
decisions.rejected: Add only the new row

decisions.decision: A dispatch contract for the engine stage (gap 10)
decisions.ruling: Dropped by the user's 'cut to the minimum' ruling (2026-11-28): no sixth dispatch contract. The stage table of plugins/vwf/assets/execute-stages.md gets an `engine` row whose note points to skills/execute/references/review-unit.md and agents/execute-engine.md, as the `run` row's note does, and the count of dispatch contracts stays five.
decisions.rejected: A note like the `run` row's, the count staying five

decisions.decision: The form of the p:plugins:check gate line (gap 11)
decisions.ruling: Every unit's line is `mise x -- mise run p:plugins:check`, the form of the plan's other gate lines.
decisions.rejected: The bare `mise run p:plugins:check`

decisions.decision: Known risks of the minimal plan
decisions.ruling: Recorded for the first real `/vwf:execute all` run that reaches a review row, not proven in this run: (a) the engine's own git commands read the worktree after the agent's cd; (b) /code-review's own agents run at layer 3 under all; (c) a hung engine hangs the run (no timer). index.md lists them under Known risks.
decisions.rejected: Prove each in this run (the D9 check, the 30-minute TaskStop wait): the user ruled 'cut to the minimum'

decisions.decision: plugins/vwf/skills/execute/SKILL.md names the engines and the five stage subagents (rulings review round 2, gap 5)
decisions.ruling: U1 owns plugins/vwf/skills/execute/SKILL.md: the `review` row at about :36 says each engine runs in its own `execute-engine` agent, and the paragraph at about :39-:43 says six stage subagents and lists `execute-engine` at review rows, once per engine.
decisions.rejected: Accept as out of scope: the skill's own entry would stay false

decisions.decision: plan-interview.md:110 and change-plan gates-consent.md:42 (rulings review round 2, gap 6)
decisions.ruling: No owner. plugins/vwf/assets/plan-interview.md:110 says the review unit 'runs /code-review and /security-review', and plugins/vwf/skills/change-plan/references/gates-consent.md:42 says a review unit 'runs /security-review and the security reviewer'. Neither says the orchestrator runs an engine in its own turn, so both stay true when an execute-engine agent runs the engine.
decisions.rejected: Widen U1 to reword them: nothing in them becomes false

decisions.decision: p:plugins:check as a unit or wave gate line (rulings review round 2, gap 7)
decisions.ruling: No change. p:plugins:check runs in the pre-commit hook of each unit commit and in code:precommit at the plan tier, so a unit or wave gate line would repeat it. Each unit's Verification still names it.
decisions.rejected: Add `mise x -- mise run p:plugins:check` to gates.unit or gates.wave
